This will be annotated in block 24 on member copy 2, 4, or 7 of the DD-Form 21 If claiming 30% Disabled Veteran, you must also submit a VA Letter or a disability determination from a branch of the Armed Forces. NOTE: All veterans claiming 10-point preference must also submit a SF-15. Current or Former Federal Civilian Employees (includes current Air Force employees): You must submit a legible copy of a SF-50, Notification of Personnel Action. The SF-50, block 24 must contain "1" or "2" AND block 34 must be a "1". Employees eligible under an OPM approved interchange agreement, block 34 may contain a "1" or "2". Promotion Consideration: If you wish to be considered as a promotion candidate and your SF-50 has an effective date within the past year, it may not clearly demonstrate you meet the one-year time-in-grade requirements. You will need to provide additional SF-50s which clearly demonstrates you meet the time-in-grade requirements (examples of appropriate SF-50s include Promotions, Within-Grade, Grade/Range Increases, and SF-50s with an effective date more than one year old). ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: The VOW Act requires federal agencies to treat an eligible active duty service member as a veteran, disabled veteran, and preference eligible (as applicable) when applying for civil service positions before the effective release or discharge date. Appointment of military members before the release or discharge date is permissible if the member is on terminal leave. At the time the active duty member applies for a civil position, he or she must submit a "certification" memo in lieu of a DD-Form 214, Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty. Active duty members applying for a civil service position without submitting a valid certification memo or DD-Form 214 with their application will render the member ineligible for the position. The certification memo must originate from the member's military service branch on official letterhead and contain the following: Name/Rank/Grade of Service Member Branch of Armed Forces Dates of Active Service (Start and End Date(s) Expected Date of Discharge/Release from Active Duty Terminal leave start date (if applicable) Expected character of service (honorable or general) and type of separation (i.e. separation or retirement) Must be certified within 120 days of anticipated discharge Signature by, or by direction of the adjutant, personnel office, unit commander, or higher headquarters commander. Note: The VOW Act provides tentative preference. If appointed, a DD Form-214 must be submitted upon receipt. OPTIONAL DOCUMENTS:
Performance Appraisals for Current Federal Civilian Employees - Most recent performance appraisals (dated within last 3 years) showing the official rating of record, signed by a supervisor, or statement why the performance appraisal is unavailable.
Awards for Current Federal Civilian Employees - List any awards received within the last 3 years on the resume.
Note: Applicant must not submit award SF50s-Notification of Personnel Actions (SF50s).

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as Sr. S&T Program Analyst at NAVAL INTELLIGENCE ACTIVITY. Drive innovation executing S&T portfolio spanning ocean engineering, unmanned vehicles, robotics, artificial intelligence, acoustics, sensing, signal processing. All Defense Intelligence positions under the Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System (DCIPS) are in the excepted service by specific statute, 10 U.S.C. 1601. This position is in the excepted service and does not confer competitive status.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will lead and execute project management functions across the technology life-cycle.

You will work with stakeholders to assess capability gaps, develop technology roadmaps and investment strategies, proposing and developing project plans, oversee project execution and develop technology transition plans.
You will advise senior leadership regarding resources to maximize projects.
You will plan and manage elements of an applied research and development portfolio that aligns with intelligence collection requirements, capabilities, and multi-year execution strategy.
You will coordinate with financial management and contracting staffs throughout project execution.
You lead and motivate project teams to ensure requirements are fully aligned with organizational needs.

You will serve as a Contracting Officer's Representative with responsibilities to include budgeting, preparing statements of work, supporting contracting processes, developing milestone drive schedules, assessing and mitigating risk.
You will monitor and report on technical progress.
Details.Evaluations: In order to qualify for this position, your resume must provide sufficient experience and/or education, knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the duties of the specific position for which you are being considered. Your resume is the key means we have for evaluating your skills, knowledge, and abilities as they relate to this position. Therefore, we encourage you to be clear and specific when describing your experience. When the application process is complete, we will review your resume to ensure you meet the hiring eligibility and qualification requirements listed in this announcement. You will be rated based on the information provided in your resume and responses to the Occupational Questionnaire, along with your supporting documentation to determine your ability to demonstrate the following competencies: ANALYTICAL CONCEPTS, POLICIES, AND PRINCIPLESANALYTICAL TECHNIQUESORAL COMMUNICATIONPROBLEM SOLVINGREPORTING AND RECOMMENDATIONSWRITTEN COMMUNICATION If after reviewing your resume and supporting documentation, a determination is made that you inflated your qualifications and/or experience, your score may be adjusted to more accurately reflect your abilities or you may be found ineligible/not qualified. If selected, you may be required to provide supporting documentation. Please follow all instructions carefully. Errors or omissions may affect your rating or consideration for employment. All eligibility, qualifications, and time-in-grade requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
MajorDuties: Oversee development of Command, Control, Communications, Computers and Intelligence (C4I) solutions on behalf of U.S. Partner Nations.
Develop acquisition plans that identify all actions and required information related to a phase of the equipment development/acquisition process.
Review program progress against plans and restructures program schedules, events, plans, and reporting requirements to better fulfill program goals.
Serve as a Contracting Officer Representative for assigned contracts and coordinates contractual issues with contracting officers and Defense Contract Management Command representatives.
Review and consolidate budget estimates from project engineers and develop justifications for costs identified.
Review execution of support contracts ensuring the scope of work is performed within budgetary guidelines.
Provide senior-level recommendations concerning contractual issues to higher management.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: *COVID-19 has severely limited available child care services in the Stuttgart Military Community. At this time, and for the foreseeable future, only the children of military service members can be accommodated in on-base child care facilities. In addition, in some Stuttgart-area communities, host-nation child care providers are not able to accommodate the children of U.S. Citizens in their programs. Applicants with child care requirements are encouraged to research options prior to accepting job offers. Child care needs will not be a factor in the selection process.* United States Africa Command USAFRICOM, is one of six geographic combatant commands and is responsible to the Secretary of Defense for military relations with African nations, the African Union, and African regional security organizations. Responsible for all operations, exercises, and security cooperation on the African continent. The mission of USAFRICOM, in concert with interagency and international partners, is to build defense capabilities, respond to crisis, and deter and defeat transnational threats in order to advance U.S. national interests and promote regional security, stability, and prosperity. USAFRICOM recognizes a diverse workforce as our differences in life experiences and cultural backgrounds brings us together by promoting innovative solutions towards common goals. We encourage talented individuals from all communities and segments of our society to apply.
MajorDuties: Provide recommendations for operations planning of contingencies and crisis actions to management, operators and staff action officers.
Assist the Functional Manager in developing and implementing Joint Operations Planning and Executions (JOPES) and Adaptive Planning and Execution (APEX) policies and procedures for the command.

Serve as Functional Manager (FM) for the Joint Capabilities Requirements Manager (JCRM) database while creating and managing accounts, updating and maintaining JCRM reference data, and providing informal training and local help-desk support to users.

Track sourcing of all US Africa Command Request for Forces for emergent, rotational, and contingency force requirements with their associated Joint Operations Planning and Execution System (JOPES) sourcing data and status.

Conduct strategic country planning in coordination with EUCOM Country Desk Officers, ODCs, BAOs, State Partnership Coordinators, various EUCOM staff entities, Service Components, and other governmental agencies for the development of the annual plan.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position serves as the Liaison Officer for the Joint Special Operations Command. This position is located in Stuttgart, Germany.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. COVID-19 has severely limited available child care services in the Stuttgart Military Community. At this time, and for the foreseeable future, only the children of military service members can be accommodated in on-base child care facilities. In addition, in some Stuttgart-area communities, host-nation child care providers are not able to accommodate the children of U.S. Citizens in their programs. Applicants with child care requirements are encouraged to research options prior to accepting job offers. Child care needs will not be a factor in the selection process. United States Africa Command (USAFRICOM), is one of six U.S. Department of Defense' geographic combatant commands and is responsible to the Secretary of Defense for military relations with African nations, the African Union, and African regional security organizations. It is responsible for all DoD operations, exercises, and security cooperation on the African continent, its island nations, and surrounding waters. Its mission is to build defense capabilities, respond to crisis, and deter and defeat transnational threats in order to advance U.S. national interests and promote regional security, stability, and prosperity.
MajorDuties: Direct interaction between command elements and external organizations for required military deception (MILDEC) planning assistance, studies, and analysis.
Consult and coordinate with service providers and other supporting organizations.
Lead joint working groups through the development of analysis, planning, deception estimates, and plans/concepts to solve complex and technical problems.
Integrate the military deception (MILDEC) discipline into the command and subordinate commands.
Develop command policy and procedures for the handling, review, and approval of military deception (MILDEC) plans based on Department of Defense (DoD) and joint guidance.

Represent the command USAFRICOM at events such as joint and service planning/working groups, meetings, conferences, briefings, and seminars related to program planning, target assessments, demonstrations of new systems, and support system concepts.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serve as a senior program analyst for Headquarters, United States European Command (USEUCOM), Directorate for Manpower and Personnel (ECJ1), under the Chief, Command and Personnel Programs Branch (ECJ1-HP). Provides support to the Branch Chief by conducting studies, analyses, and evaluations of major personnel programs and policy issues across the Department of Defense (DoD), the major Service components, and other governmental activities and agencies as required.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. This position is located in Stuttgart, Germany. Stuttgart is the cultural and political capital of Baden-Wuerttemberg and one of Europe's foremost metropolitan areas. Stuttgart is charmingly situated in the heart of one of Germany's largest wine-growing regions, attracting tourists by its magnificent panorama, its impressive gardens and parks, palaces and buildings in a wide range of architectural styles, but also by its cultural diversity. The city of Stuttgart comprises five counties encompassing 179 towns and rural districts. It is the home to USAG Stuttgart, HQ US EUCOM, HQ US AFRICOM, and other tenant units. Please note: COVID-19 has severely limited available childcare services in the Stuttgart Military Community. At this time, and for the foreseeable future, only the children of military service members can be accommodated in on-base child care facilities. In addition, in some Stuttgart-area communities, host-nation childcare providers are not able to accommodate the children of U.S. Citizens in their programs. Applicants with child care requirements are encouraged to research options prior to accepting job offers. Child care needs will not be a factor in the selection process.
MajorDuties: Facilitate teams which review existing programs and using programmatic and financial data as a basis, recommends program initiation, termination, modification or enhancement to meet the needs of service members and their families.
Integrate personnel program policy into larger ECJ1, USEUCOM, Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) and Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD) planning efforts. Serve as acting Branch Chief in their absence.
Provide analytical foresight on DoD data worksheets used to justify entitlements with field, JCS and OSD representatives.
Consolidate requests and coordinate with JCS and OSD representatives until published in the Financial Management Regulation (FMR).

Determine the appropriate number of contingency postal operation locations, mail transportation networks, the type of Military Postal Service (MPS) support to be provided, and all other MPS functional areas.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: You will serve as a Protocol Specialist in the United States European Command (USEUCOM) Protocol Office. Act as a USEUCOM point of contact for allied military and civilian organizations for visits and protocol matters. Perform a wide variety of duties, to include coordination with the visitor or the visitor's staff of individuals who visit USEUCOM to serve as briefer or in support of the command.
Details.SubAgencyName: Headquarters United States European Command, Protocol Office
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement:
Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential.
This position is located in Stuttgart, Germany. Stuttgart is the cultural and political capital of Baden-Wuerttemberg and one of Europe's foremost metropolitan areas. Stuttgart is charmingly situated in the heart of one of Germany's largest wine-growing regions, attracting tourists by its magnificent panorama, its impressive gardens and parks, palaces and buildings in a wide range of architectural styles, but also by its cultural diversity. For additional information please visit https://home.army.mil/stuttgart/
Please note: COVID-19 has severely limited available childcare services in the Stuttgart Military Community. At this time, and for the foreseeable future, only the children of military service members can be accommodated in on-base child care facilities. In addition, in some Stuttgart-area communities, host-nation childcare providers are not able to accommodate the children of U.S. Citizens in their programs.
MajorDuties: Provide close coordination with the visiting dignitary or the dignitary's staff, including military flag officers, ambassadors, and high level officials in local and international governments, and with external civilian agencies.
Manage the day to day USEUCOM Commander's Official Representation Gift Locker and the legal parameters for usage of the Secretary of the Army Official Representational funds (ORF).
Participate in planning USEUCOM protocol policies and procedures for conducting major meetings and visitations.
Provide host nation guidance, advisory services and support for USEUCOM HQs.
Maintain the protocol library on social usage, protocol, congressional directories, general officer rosters, travel guides, billeting, and restaurant information.
Develop recommended itineraries, instructions, guides, supplementary material, and pertinent correspondence.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: You will serve as Assistant Secretary of the Joint Staff for the Headquarters (HQ) U.S. European Command (USEUCOM) Office of the Secretary of the Joint Staff (SJS), supporting the 4-star USEUCOM Commander. Provide a full range of management support including staff counsel, administrative expertise, program management, and analytical functions essential to the direction and operation of the USEUCOM command group and staff.
Details.SubAgencyName: Headquarters United States European Command,  Secretary to the Joint Staff
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement:
Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This position is located in Stuttgart, Germany. Stuttgart is the cultural and political capital of Baden-Wuerttemberg and one of Europe's foremost metropolitan areas. Stuttgart is charmingly situated in the heart of one of Germany's largest wine-growing regions, attracting tourists by its magnificent panorama, its impressive gardens and parks, palaces and buildings in a wide range of architectural styles, but also by its cultural diversity. For additional information please visit https://home.army.mil/stuttgart/
Please note: COVID-19 has severely limited available childcare services in the Stuttgart Military Community. At this time, and for the foreseeable future, only the children of military service members can be accommodated in on-base child care facilities. In addition, in some Stuttgart-area communities, host-nation childcare providers are not able to accommodate the children of U.S. Citizens in their programs.
MajorDuties: Serve as a Principal Advisor to the Secretary of the Joint Staff (SJS); and advisor to the Deputy Commander, Chief of Staff, Deputy Chief of Staff, and Headquarters staff.

Represent the SJS and exercises full authority in addressing administrative issues, resolving problems and providing recommendations to senior leadership for correcting or improving administrative functions.

Provide full range of management support including staff counsel, administrative expertise, program management, and analytical functions essential to the direction and operation of the USEUCOM command group and staff.
Manage cost, schedule, and performance of SJS contracts, and serve as a performance monitor and quality assurance evaluator for contracts.
Manage the planning, development, implementation, operations and maintenance of the tasker management tool (TMT) to administer and track internal and external command actions.
Establish internal procedures to secure adequate control of taskers, deadlines, progress reports, and directives.

Plan and prepare executive level events and meetings in coordination with USEUCOM Command Group, SHAPE Special Assistants, Directorates, Special Staff, and USEUCOM Component Command staffs to facilitate executive dialogue.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is located in Stuttgart, Germany. Stuttgart is the cultural and political capital of Baden-Wuerttemberg and one of Europe's foremost metropolitan areas. The city of Stuttgart comprises five counties encompassing 179 towns and rural districts. It is the home to USAG Stuttgart, HQ US EUCOM, HQ US AFRICOM, and other tenant units. For additional information please visit https://home.army.mil/stuttgart.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. COVID-19 has severely limited available child care services in the Stuttgart Military Community. At this time, and for the foreseeable future, only the children of military service members can be accommodated in on-base child care facilities. In addition, in some Stuttgart-area communities, host-nation child care providers are not able to accommodate the children of U.S. Citizens in their programs. Applicants with child care requirements are encouraged to research options prior to accepting job offers. Child care needs will not be a factor in the selection process. United States Africa Command (USAFRICOM), is one of six U.S. Department of Defense' geographic combatant commands and is responsible to the Secretary of Defense for military relations with African nations, the African Union, and African regional security organizations. It is responsible for all DoD operations, exercises, and security cooperation on the African continent, its island nations, and surrounding waters. Its mission is to build defense capabilities, respond to crisis, and deter and defeat transnational threats in order to advance U.S. national interests and promote regional security, stability, and prosperity.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is located in Stuttgart, Germany. Stuttgart is charmingly situated in the heart of one of Germany's largest wine-growing regions, attracting tourists by its magnificent panorama, impressive gardens and parks, and palaces and buildings in a wide range of architectural styles. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. COVID-19 has severely limited available child care services in the Stuttgart Military Community. At this time, and for the foreseeable future, only the children of military service members can be accommodated in on-base child care facilities. In addition, in some Stuttgart-area communities, host-nation child care providers are not able to accommodate the children of U.S. Citizens in their programs. Applicants with child care requirements are encouraged to research options prior to accepting job offers. Child care needs will not be a factor in the selection process. United States Africa Command (USAFRICOM), is one of six U.S. Department of Defense' geographic combatant commands and is responsible to the Secretary of Defense for military relations with African nations, the African Union, and African regional security organizations. It is responsible for all DoD operations, exercises, and security cooperation on the African continent, its island nations, and surrounding waters. Its mission is to build defense capabilities, respond to crisis, and deter and defeat transnational threats in order to advance U.S. national interests and promote regional security, stability, and prosperity.
MajorDuties: Articulate and communicate assignments to branch employees, projects problems to be solved, identifies actionable events, milestones, and/or program issues under review, and deadlines and time frames for completion.
Develop and review implementation of an effective, reliable, long range exercise program that will be systematically and periodically updated.
Develop, implement, and manage a multi-million dollar exercise budget, tasks and evaluates personnel, and enforces Management Internal Controls.

Provide guidance to support development and execution of headquarters and multi-national exercises in support of U.S. national military strategy and regional requirements for USAFRICOM and Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) directed exercises.

Lead the joint exercise branch in planning, coordination and synchronization of all USAFRICOM and service component commands exercises; is responsible for all exercise information and support tasking messages.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is in the ECJ38 Integrated Air and Missile Defense Division. The primary duties of this position are to lead operational planning to execute integrated air and missile defense (IAMD) operations within the U.S. European Command (USEUCOM) area of responsibility (AOR) to secure the U.S Homeland, USEUCOM forces, NATO, and allied forces/interests, to include allies in support of national global objectives.
Details.SubAgencyName: Headquarters United States European Command, ECJ3 OPERATIONS DIRECTORATE
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement:
Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This position is located in Stuttgart, Germany. Stuttgart is the cultural and political capital of Baden-Wuerttemberg and one of Europe's foremost metropolitan areas. Stuttgart is charmingly situated in the heart of one of Germany's largest wine-growing regions, attracting tourists by its magnificent panorama, its impressive gardens and parks, palaces and buildings in a wide range of architectural styles, but also by its cultural diversity. For additional information please visit https://home.army.mil/stuttgart/
Please note: COVID-19 has severely limited available childcare services in the Stuttgart Military Community. At this time, and for the foreseeable future, only the children of military service members can be accommodated in on-base child care facilities. In addition, in some Stuttgart-area communities, host-nation childcare providers are not able to accommodate the children of U.S. Citizens in their programs.
MajorDuties: Analyze political, military, economic, social information, and infrastructure (PMESII) factors influencing military and political strategy.
Provide inputs and advice on IAMD planning, integration and execution matters; specifically integration of Offensive and Defensive counter-air concepts in accordance with JP 3-01.
Prepare and present multimedia presentation information briefings, reports and staff action packages for command-level audiences.
Distill key data points from acquisition programs, development, funding and operational plans, and reports.
Research and integrate analytical expertise to integrate USEUCOM regional strategies into the operational planning and crisis action planning processes.

Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management web site: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a SUPERVISORY PROGRAM ANALYST in the FLEET Modernization and Facilities Management Directorate of NAVAL INFORMATION FORCES.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will interpret and implement Fleet Commander C5I modernization and maintenance guidance and processes.

You will demonstrate exceptional leadership, decision-making, analytical, and evaluative skills and capacity to carry out original and creative work in the areas of planning modernization and integration planning of complex C5I systems.

You will establish and maintain working relationships with top agency senior DOD, DON, and SYSCOMs representatives to provide guidance and assistance on a wide variety of C5I Information Warfare issues and concerns.
You will be responsible for coordination and integration of several complex programs with major technical aspects that provide integrated C5ISR and IW capabilities to the Navy and Joint warfighters.
You will make major decisions that have a substantial impact on the Fleet and the command?s field commands.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as the Staff Protocol Specialist and Administrative Assistant to the Chief of Staff (CoS), providing advice and training on matters relating to customs and regulations governing diplomatic formality and etiquette. You will coordinate a wide range of executive support level functions including conference management, calendar maintenance, correspondence preparation and review, and travel coordination. This position is located at NAVY INFORMATION FORCES in Suffolk, VA.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will provide direct support to the Commander, Deputy Commander, Chief of Staff, and NAVIFOR Staff regarding protocol matters.
You will provide direction and coordination to NAVIFOR Staff members and representatives of subordinate commands, as required, to plan and execute programs and visits.
You will oversee and coordinate day-to-day executive administrative operations and NAVIFOR executive staff efforts.
You will prioritize, develop, assemble, and review appropriate daily briefing books, memorandums, and information/read-ahead packages.
You will prepare read-ahead documents, schedule video teleconferences, and reserve conference rooms for meetings.

Details.JobSummary: This position is part of the Organization of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. The incumbent will be responsible for serves as the APFDD Branch Head for Foreign Liaison Officer (FLO) integration Branch and functions as Representative of Division Chief.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement:
This position is located in the J-7, Joint Force Development Directorate (DJ-7), Deputy Directorate Joint Warfighting Development (DD JWD), Allies and Partners Force Development Division (APFDD), and reports directly to the APFDD Chief and DD JWD. APFDD coordinates, integrates, and expands bilateral partner nations and U.S. Alliances into the Joint Staff (JS) joint force development and design activities on behalf of the Chairman of the Joint
Chief of Staff (CJCS) and DJ-7. APFDD leads specified multinational force development initiatives that strengthen coalition capabilities and enable globally integrated operations through these partnerships.
MajorDuties: As a SUPERVISORY FOREIGN LIAISON (INTERNATIONAL PROGRAMS) at the GS-0301-15 some of your typical work assignments may include: Serves as senior international policy and technical expert, analyst, and advisor to the Division Chief on a broad spectrum of Allies and Partner Integration issues, international organizational, managerial, capability development, and technical issues related to Division operations. Leads DoD effort for establishing and maintaining bilateral Memoranda of Agreement/Understanding (MOAs/MOUs) at the direction of OSD Policy. These legally binding international agreements allows the appropriate exchange of information between J-7 and multiple bilateral partners and support all foreign postings from the 21 nations assigned to J-7 throughout the U.S. services, combatant commanders and their components. Leads and develops guidance for comprehensive management analyses that improves the overall integration and enhancement of the international program into the daily operations for J-7 and the Joint Staff. Represents the Joint Staff and J-7 at senior key leader exchanges. These events include visits from senior Allied and partner nation visits to the Joint Staff in both the Pentagon and Suffolk, as well as J-7 leadership engagements with counterparts in 21 Allied and partner nations. Establishes and maintains liaison with professional groups, DoD, and other government agencies to gain insights and support to improve J-7 training and joint force development performance. Oversees the coordination with US Contact Officers assigned to each foreign officers assigned throughout the JS to ensure all training and certifications are current and properly reported to the JS Multinational Working Group in accordance with DoD/Joint Staff regulatory requirements. Exercises management responsibility for assigned programs and functions, assumes technical direction for front-end analyses required to define management and multinational force issues, and develops those issues into comprehensive requirements and programs of work. Exercises supervisory and delegated managerial authority and operational direction in establishing goals and objectives and their implementation for a staff of professionals within the Branch and assists the Division Chief when away on official business for Division taskings.

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: Serve as a Management Analyst specializing in Manpower within as assigned Defense Health Agency's (DHA's) Region or Large Market Office for the Puget Sound Market Office.
Details.SubAgencyName: DHA Puget Sound Market, Resource Operations, Manpowers
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: At the Defense Health Agency (DHA), our Mission is to support the National Defense Strategy and Service Military Departments by leading the Military Health System (MHS) as an integrated, highly reliable system of medical training, readiness, and health. As the health care delivery arm of the MHS, DHA is crucial to supporting the Department of Defense's integrated system of readiness and health. DHA manages a global health care network of military and civilian medical professionals and more than 400 military hospitals and clinics around the world. DHA is a joint, integrated Combat Support Agency that enables the Army, Navy, and Air Force medical services to provide a medically ready force and ready medical force to Combatant Commands in both peacetime and wartime. The DHA supports the delivery of integrated, affordable, and high quality health services to the MHS beneficiaries and is responsible for driving greater integration of clinical and business processes across the MHS.
MajorDuties: Provide expert level consultation, support, and assistance to the Market Office and Medical Treatment Facility Directors, and key staff on DHA initiatives for the purpose of maintain a capable medical workforce throughout the Market Area.

Serve as principal advisor and technical expert in the areas of manpower, force management, force structure, manpower staffing criteria, the distribution and documentation of manpower resources, and the Direct Health Care Provider Program.
Serve as the Puget Sound Market technical advisor on the DHA?s Automated Staffing Assessment Model (ASAM) utilized for manpower requirements determination.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: With a workforce of more than 13,000 reflecting our nation's diverse cultures and backgrounds, and annual sales of more than $4.5M, the Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) operates a worldwide chain of 236 commissaries providing groceries to active-duty military families, retirees and their families, DeCA employees, and other authorized patrons in a safe and secure shopping environment. A core military family support element and a valued part of military pay and benefits, commissaries contribute to family readiness, enhance the quality of life for America's military and their families, and help recruit and retain the best and brightest men and women to serve our country.
MajorDuties: Serves as the Computer Assisted Ordering Technician in a Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) location. The primary purpose of this position is to maintain accurate perpetual inventory balance on hand (BOH) levels which in turn determines optimum ordering quantities and ensures product availability for patrons. Position responsibilities include: Maintains the Computer Assisted Ordering (CAO) system with current, accurate data to ensure optimal order quantities are calculated necessary to sustain customer demands. Uses radio-frequency hand-held terminals to gather data necessary to update and adjust inventory. Records and updates Balance on Hand (BOH) data; maintains perpetual inventory and audits credits. Performs daily inventory audit of items not-in-stock and overwrite items. Evaluates stock levels of all CAO categories daily by physically reviewing the storage and display shelf locations, shippers and warehouse. Interfaces with all levels of management and deals directly with commercial distributor/vendor stocking representatives on issues affecting CAO.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary:
To qualify for a Management Analyst, your resume and supporting documentation must support: Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience that equipped you with the particular competencies to successfully perform the duties of the position and is directly in or related to this position. To qualify at the GS-09 level, applicants must possess one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-07 level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service, military or private sector. To qualify at the GS-07 level, applicants must possess one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-05 level or equivalent under other pay systems in the Federal service, military or private sector. Applicants must meet eligibility requirements including time-in-grade (General Schedule (GS) positions only), time-after-competitive appointment, minimum qualifications, and any other regulatory requirements by the cut-off/closing date of the announcement. Creditable specialized experience includes: GS-07: Assisting with identifying issues or problems of a procedural or factual nature. Reviewing information and determining which administrative guidelines should be applied. Reviewing processes to ensure requirements of assigned projects are met. GS-09: Analyzing and evaluating issues to identify, consider, and resolve problems of a procedural or factual nature; Providing administrative support for common workplace procedures, such as monitoring suspenses, reporting, training support, telework management, employee surveys, and timekeeping. Utilizing procedures and regulations to ensure administrative submissions conform to requirements. Reviewing standard operating procedures and making recommendations to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of existing processes. OR B. Education Substitution: Such education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work. Education must be from a college or university accredited by an organization approved by the U.S. Department of Education. See http://ope.ed.gov/accreditation/Search.aspx. If using education to meet basic qualifications, YOU MUST SUBMIT A TRANSCRIPT as supplemental documentation. To qualify based on education in lieu of specialized experience, you must possess: GS-09: master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.B. or J.D., if related.
GS-07: 1 full year of graduate level education or superior academic achievement OR C. Combination: Combinations of successfully completed post-high school education and experience may be used to meet total qualification requirements for grade levels GS-09 and GS-07, and may be computed by first determining the applicant's total qualifying experience as a percentage of the experience required for the grade level; then determining the applicant's education as a percentage of the education required for the grade level; and then adding the two percentages. The total percentages must equal at least 100 percent to qualify an applicant for that grade level. Only graduate education in excess of the amount required for the next lower grade level may be used to qualify applicants for positions at grade GS-09 and GS-07.

Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes providing administrative assistance in support of a military unit or military activity in one or more of the following areas: Unit or individual training, medical readiness, personnel actions, financial actions, supply, or logistics; performing day-to-day administrative functions; and preparing or reviewing written products. Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This is a Military Technician position with the 377th Theater Sustainment Command, 639 Transportation DET, 1397 Deployment Distribution Support Battalion, 1394 Transportation Support Brigade, Deployment Support Command located at Vallejo, California. This position requires an active membership as a Soldier in the Army Reserve before a start date can be set. To learn more about minimum qualifications to join the Army Reserve, visit http://www.goarmy.com/reserve/jobs.html
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This is a Military Technician position with the US Army Reserves. Becoming a Military Technician allows you to experience the best of two worlds by taking advantage of the opportunity to become a Citizen Soldier in the US Army Reserve Military Technician program. This enables you to receive full civil service benefits and military reserve benefits. Military Technicians are a vital link between the US Army Reserves and civil service and are one of the most important keys to combat readiness.
MajorDuties: Manage the daily operations of a US Army Reserve unit's mission readiness program.
Represent the US Army Reserve Troop Program Unit Commander in his/her absence.
Perform as the record manager.
Serve as the unit physical security coordinator.
Review regulations and directives and implements changes in appropriate manner.
Compile data and create products to present at briefings.
Prepare and review command correspondence for content and accuracy.
Manage unit and individual personnel and medical readiness.
Execute the unit's supply and logistics program.
Coordinate the management of unit and individual training readiness.
Administer financial management program including Government Purchasing and Travel Card programs.
Advise on pay, benefits, entitlements, incentives, and assist with correcting pay issues.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. Vicenza is a beautiful city steeped in rich history, with a wealth of cultural, recreational and entertainment opportunities. Located about 45 minutes west of Venice and within a few hours drive of Austria, Switzerland and world-renowned Italian cities, most of the American military community works on Caserma Ederle, located just east of downtown Vicenza. It is home to the U.S. Army Africa headquarters, part of the 173rd Infantry Brigade Combat Team (Airborne), other tenant units and the U.S. Army Garrison Italy headquarters. Are you interested in helping to defend our Nation? Exciting career opportunities are available with the U.S. Army Network Enterprise Technology Command (NETCOM)!

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. This position is located in Vilseck, Germany. The town of Vilseck is situated on the river Vils ('eck' in German means corner and so Vilseck is on a corner or edge of the Vils), a tributary of the Naab river. The Grafenwoehr Training Area complex (GTA) is a live-fire multi-national shooting range and borders the town of Vilseck on the north. The town is home to Germany's first tower museum. The ancient Bavarian village of Vilseck is geographically completely separate from the nearby large American military base which is commonly referred to by the same name. Our communities are truly communities of excellence. The local German communities of Grafenwoehr and Vilseck are rich in history and offer many activities and opportunities for the whole family to enjoy. For additional information please visit www.grafenwoehr.army.mil.
MajorDuties: Conduct prevention activities in an effort to reduce or eliminate sexual harassment and sexual assault.
Ensure that sexual assault victim advocacy services are available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, both on and off post, for all service members and other persons covered by the SHARP Program.
Conduct response activities in the event of a sexual harassment complaint or sexual assault.
Plan, organize, staff, carry out reviews and evaluate a positive management oriented SHARP program that includes efforts to resolve systemic problems.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary:
In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Miscellaneous Administration and Program, 0301. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-09, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes knowledge of simulator operations, JTAC communications and targeting equipment utilized during CAS planning and execution, scenario development, distributed training networks, network security and training network standards. Knowledge of specialized subject matter or program areas for the operations, products, services, needs, and goals of programs and other organizations serviced to develop original designs, concepts, or visual styles in a joint training environment, exhibits, or presentation materials that present the ideas or image desired by the organization, that are used in simulation training environment, or that reduce the cost of production, installation, or maintenance of the visual product. EDUCATION: Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position. NOTE: You must submit a copy of transcripts. OR LL.M., if related. NOTE: You must submit a copy of transcripts OR
COMBINATION OF EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION: A combination of education and experience may be used to qualify for this position as long as the computed percentage of the requirements is at least 100%. NOTE: You must submit a copy of transcripts. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in­-grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-09 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-11 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Working knowledge of simulator operations, JTAC communications and targeting equipment utilized during CAS planning and execution, scenario development, distributed training networks, network security and training network standards. 2. Working knowledge of sister service fires capabilities, to a level that they are able to mimic all rotary and fixed wing techniques, tactics and procedures for all services. 3. Skill in designing and conducting comprehensive training programs, and preparing solutions to resolve substantive problems and issues of effectiveness and efficiency related to unit training systems and their application. 4. Ability to maintain an up-to-date awareness of technological advances and predict how management can meet future requirements. Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing; problem solve complex issues and maintain good working relationships. 5. Knowledge of network security requirements and techniques for protecting computer and simulator systems from viruses, data tampering, and unauthorized system entry. Knowledge of a full range of network systems "LAN/WAN" design principles, methodologies, and approaches used in developing, installing, operating, managing, maintaining network services that support functional requirements, and security (and IT) procedures to maintain control of classified material. 6. Knowledge of the network architecture, interrelationships, operating modes, configuration, topology, and protocols typically found at root level. Knowledge of network operating and maintenance concepts and methods to troubleshoot network problems. Knowledge of complex configuration management techniques, and requirements appropriate to managing root level network systems. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite! This position is a DoD Cyber Excepted Service (CES) personnel system position in the Excepted Service under 10 U.S.C. 1599f.
MajorDuties: You will serve as the civilian personnel liaison for all civilian personnel matters with various Human Resources Offices (HROs) and office of Civilian Human resources (OCHRs) that support the command.
You will prepare requests for personnel actions and track and verify the action requested using the Defense Civilian Personnel data System (DCPDS) and associated software.

You will review requests for personnel actions ensuring requests are complete, accurate, approved by the designated authority and appropriate in accordance with civilian personnel regulations and command policies.
You will review position descriptions (PDs) for civilian positions at the command and regional activities.
You will provide civilian personnel data in support of recurring budget data calls and taskings.
You will assist civilian personnel in obtaining answers to their questions regarding benefits, retirement, open season, pay and leave usage.
You will assist management with the performance management program and ensure appraisals are completed and submitted in a timely and accurate manner.
You will provide in-briefs to new employee check-ins and ensure personnel leaving the command have an opportunity to complete an exit interview.

You should expect that we will verify performance, suitability, and security information and take that information into account in making employment offers. NOTE: Due to COVID19, if you have any questions or need assistance, please email the DON Employment Information Center at DONEIC@us.navy.mil
Details.RequiredDocuments:
A complete resume is required. Your resume must show relevant experience, job title, duties and accomplishments. Your resume must show complete information for each job entry to support minimum qualifications. The following information should be provided in your resume, but it is acceptable to provide elsewhere in your application package: employer's name, starting and end dates (Mo/Yr), hours per week, and pay plan, series and grade level (e.g. GS-0201-09) for relevant federal experience.TIP: A good way to ensure you include all essential information is to use the Resume Builder in USAJOBS to create your resume. Are you claiming membership in any professional organizations, or possession of a license, certificate or credentials? Check the Conditions of Employment section above to see if any are required. If you claim membership, license, certification, or credentials, you must submit a copy of said document in your application package. Are you using education as a substitute for some or all of the experience requirement? Is there a basic education requirement for this position? Check the Education section above to see what is allowed and what is required. Any claims you make in your resume or assessment questionnaire regarding education or degrees MUST be supported by submitting with your application official or unofficial transcripts or a list of courses, grades earned, completion dates, and quarter and semester hours earned issued from your school. While unofficial transcripts are acceptable for initial application, an official transcript will ultimately be required if you are selected for the position. You may submit a copy your degree(s) if specific coursework does not have to be verified. Are you a veteran claiming 5-point veterans' preference or claiming sole survivorship preference? You must submit a copy of your latest DD-214 Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty (any copy that shows all dates of service, as well as character of service [Honorable, General, etc.] is acceptable) OR a VA letter that shows dates of service or service connected disability AND character of service. If you have more than one DD-214 for multiple periods of active duty service, submit a copy for each period of service. If you were issued a DD-215 to amend aforementioned information on the DD-214 you must submit that too. If you are not sure of your preference eligibility, visit the Department of Labor's website: Veterans' Preference Advisor Are you a disabled veteran or claiming 10-point veterans' preference?
If you are eligible to claim 10 point veterans preference you must submit a DD-214 Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty as described above for 5-point preference. You must also provide the applicable supporting documentation of your disability (e.g. disability letter from the VA) as described on Standard Form-15 (SF-15). http://www.opm.gov/forms/pdf_fill/SF15.pdf. Are you an active duty service member? Active Duty Service Members are required to submit a statement of service printed on command letterhead and signed by the command. The statement of service must provide the branch of service, rate/rank, all dates of service, the expected date of discharge and anticipated character of service (Honorable, General, etc.). Documents submitted as part of the application package, to include supplemental documents, may be shared beyond the Human Resources Office. Some supplemental documents contain personal information such as SSN and DOB and some documents such as military orders and marriage certificates may contain personal information for someone other than you. You may sanitize these documents to remove said personal information before you submit your application. You must provide an un-sanitized version of the documents if you are selected. DoD Components with CES positions apply Veterans' Preference to preference eligible candidates as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., in accordance with the procedures provided in DoD Instruction 1400.25, Volume 3005, "CES Employment and Placement." If you are a veteran claiming veterans' preference, as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., you must submit documents verifying your eligibility with your application package. Examples of these documents include: a DD-214 (Member-4 copy); a Statement of Service (if you are currently active duty) from your unit which states the date you entered on active duty, the date you are separating, character of service, and the campaign medals you have received. Veterans with a service-connected disability rating must submit an official written document from the Department of Veterans Affairs certifying your compensable service-connected disability rating with overall percentage clearly shown.
Details.OtherInformation: This position is covered by the Department of Defense Priority Placement Program. Several vacancies may be filled. A tentative offer of employment will be rescinded if the selectee fails to meet the pre-employment requirements, including failure to report to any of the scheduled appointments. Federal annuitant information: The selection of an annuitant is subject to the Department of Defense and Department of the Navy policy on the employment of annuitants. Policy information may be found at: http://www.secnav.navy.mil/donhr/Documents/CivilianJobs/FedCivAnnuitants.pdf. This position is in the excepted service and does not confer competitive status. This position is a DoD Cyber Excepted Service (CES) personnel system position in the Excepted Service under 10 U.S.C. 1599f. The Cyber Interagency Transfer Authority (CITA) permits movement of CES employees appointed under Section 1599f of Title 10 U.S.C. and excepted service employees appointed under Schedule A, Section 213.3106(b)(11) of Title 5 CFR, into cyber workforce positions in the competitive service and movement of competitive service employees into DoD Cyber Workforce positions within the Military Departments and Defense Agencies.

PositionSchedule.Name: Intermittent

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. Specialized Experience: Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-12 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate knowledge and an in-depth understanding of the mission objectives, apply an extensive knowledge of effective management principles and practices in conjunction with policies, regulations, and procedures of the natural disaster and emergency programs, provide knowledge of principles, concepts, and methodology, knowledge of data collection and analysis techniques to support trend analysis, review and manage assigned program development activities, program accounts, and projects. Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-12).

Details.JobSummary: About the Position: This position is part of the Reemployed Annuitants Cadre. Employees occupying these positions will provide emergency support to disaster stricken areas throughout the United States. Employee must pass a stringent medical screening and be prepared to live and work in extremely austere conditions. This position is a temp position for 1 year, however at the discretion of management the position may be converted to a term position up to a maximum NTE 4 years.
Details.SubAgencyName: HQ, US Army Corps of Engineers-Reemployed Annuitant Program Cadre
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Looking for a great place to work? The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is one of the best! In 2016, USACE ranked number two of government large-agency subcomponents! As rated by their employees, USACE supervisors strongly support employee development and opportunities to demonstrate leadership skills, while also maintaining an optimal work/life balance The Corps offers a team-inspiring and collaborative work environment; providing challenging and rewarding careers across a variety of disciplines. Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army.
MajorDuties: Serves as Program Manager with responsibility for exercising management and operational control over assigned programs within the organization.

Manages work in an organization with responsibility for overseeing development of the Corps' natural disaster and emergency program under which the Corps provides assistance to non-Department of Defense entities.
Manages program funds to ensure effective and efficient utilization.
Develops, and interprets Corps policies regarding assigned program areas.
Provides coordination with HQ, USACE staff and command group, USACE-wide management/staff, HQDA and DOD staffs, private contractors, and other Federal Agency staffs.
Details.Education: Some federal jobs allow you to substitute your education for the required experience in order to qualify. For this job, you must meet the qualification requirement using experience alone--no substitution of education for experience is permitted.
Details.Evaluations: Once the announcement has closed, a review of your application package (resume, supporting documents, and responses to the questionnaire) will be used to determine whether you meet the qualification requirements listed on this announcement. If you are minimally qualified, your résumé and supporting documentation will be compared against your responses to the assessment questionnaire to determine your level of experience. If, after reviewing your résumé and/or supporting documentation, a determination is made that you have inflated your qualifications and/or experience, you may lose consideration for this position. Please follow all instructions carefully when applying, errors or omissions may affect your eligibility. You should list any relevant performance appraisals and incentive awards in your resume as that information may be taken into consideration during the selection process. If selected, you may be required to provide supporting documentation. Interagency Career Transition Assistance Program (ICTAP). If you are a Federal employee in the competitive service and your agency has notified you in writing that you are a displaced employee eligible for ICTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority for this position. To receive selection priority, you must: (1) meet ICTAP eligibility criteria (2) be rated well-qualified for the position and; (3) submit the appropriate documentation to support your ICTAP eligibility. To be considered well-qualified and receive selection priority applicants must satisfy all qualification requirements for the position and receive a score of 90 or above. Additional information about the program is on OPM's Career Transition Resources website.

The complete application package must be submitted by 11:59 PM (EST) on 01/23/2023 to receive consideration. To begin, click Apply to access the online application. You will need to be logged into your USAJOBS account to apply. If you do not have a USAJOBS account, you will need to create one before beginning the application (https://apply.usastaffing.gov/ViewQuestionnaire/10911681). Follow the prompts to select your résumé and/or other supporting documents to be included with your application package. You will have the opportunity to upload additional documents to include in your application before it is submitted. Your uploaded documents may take several hours to clear the virus scan process. After acknowledging you have reviewed your application package, complete the Include Personal Information section as you deem appropriate and click to continue with the application process. You will be taken to the online application which you must complete in order to apply for the position. Complete the online application, verify the required documentation is included with your application package, and submit the application. You must re-select your resume and/or other documents from your USAJOBS account or your application will be incomplete. It is your responsibility to verify that your application package (resume, supporting documents, and responses to the questionnaire) is complete, accurate, and submitted by the closing date. Your resume: Your resume may be submitted in any format and must support the specialized experience described in this announcement. If your resume does not contain this information, your application may be marked as incomplete and you may not receive consideration for this position. For additional information see: What to include in your resume. 2. Selection is subject to restrictions resulting from Department of Defense referral system for displaced employees. If you have retired from federal service and you are interested in employment as a reemployed annuitant, see the information in the Reemployed Annuitant information sheet. If you are a Federal employee in the competitive service and your agency has notified you in writing that you are a displaced employee eligible for ICTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority. To receive selection priority for this position, you must: (1) meet ICTAP eligibility criteria; (2) be rated well-qualified for the position with a score of 90 or above; and, (3) submit the appropriate documentation to support your ICTAP eligibility. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary:
In order to qualify, you must meet the specialized experience requirements described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Administrative and Management Positions. SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have at least one (1) year of specialized experience at the next lower grade GS-07, or equivalent in other pay systems. Examples of specialized experience includes knowledge of contract regulations, policies, techniques, methods, and procedures for performing quality assurance; knowledge in interpreting blueprints and schematic drawings; and knowledge of basic handling, storage, and application of hazardous materials. OR EDUCATION: Successfully completed a master's or equivalent graduate degree or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.B or J.D. in a field which demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to perform the work of the position. NOTE: You must submit copies of your college transcripts. OR COMBINATION OF EXPERIENCE AND EDUCATION: Less than the full amount of specialized experience described in the job opportunity announcement; however, and have at least one year of progressively higher level graduate education, but have not obtained a master's or equivalent graduate degree. Therefore, have a combination of experience and education. NOTE: You must submit a copy of transcripts. FEDERAL TIME-IN-GRADE (TIG) REQUIREMENT FOR GENERAL SCHEDULE (GS) POSITIONS: Merit promotion applicants must meet applicable time-in-­grade requirements to be considered eligible. One year at the GS-07 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS-09 level. TIG applies if you are in a current GS position or held a GS position within the previous 52 weeks. NOTE: Applicants applying as VEOA candidates who are current GS civil service employees or are prior GS civil service employees within the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: 1. Knowledge of contract regulations, policies, techniques, methods, and procedures for performing quality assurance.
2. Proficient in the interpretation of blueprints and schematic drawing. Knowledgeable of basic handling, storage, and application of hazardous materials
3. Proficient in the methods used to process supply and contracted service transactions for purchases made with the GPC.
4. Skilled in the use of computer software applications integral to daily operations facilitating the completion of administrative and accounting tasks associated with contract management. Ability to review contractual documents and files to ensure contractual obligations are satisfied and that regulatory and procedural requirements are met. 5. Skilled in the effective identification of unusual or complex problems and the efficient initiations of appropriate corrective actions to resolve or mitigate problems.
6. Ability to effectively review a variety of contract actions and independently perform the assigned duties in compliance with established polices, procedures, and time frames. Skilled in the supervision of assign QAE personnel, mainlining personnel records, and evaluating personnel. Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing.

Details.JobSummary: The primary purpose of this position is to manage the activities of the Service Contract Specialist in the development and implementation of quality assurance programs for the management of the installation's Central Heat Plant, Contractor Operated Civil Engineering Supply Store, Grounds Maintenance, Refuse, Custodial Service Contracts and the Portable Latrines Blanket Purchase Agreement.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The mission of the United States Air Force is: To fly, fight, and win...Airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Global Reach and Global Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. MajorDuties: Supervises approximately 5 QAEs to ensure they perform and document inspections, coordinate with affected parties, prepare changes to contracts or purchase orders, maintains files, and investigate and resolve customer complaints. Conducts evaluation, analysis, of the subordinate QAE's contract supporting documentation to determine the consistency or the supporting contractor's compliance with their applicable service and or commodity contract requirements as cited in the Statement of Work, Service Delivery Summary, the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan, and QAP inspection checklists. Develops and presents analysis of contractor performance to the civil engineering commander and management personnel. Evaluates the inspection of service and commodity contracts. Reconciles all contract discrepancies {contract requirements performance) with the involvement of the contractor and the contracting office and Serves as the Base Civil Engineering representative for all financial requirements and responsibilities pertaining to pending and existing contracts and contract negotiations.

Transcripts/Registration/License: If qualifying on education/position requires education, you must submit copies of your transcripts and if required for the position, submit an active, current registration/license. Veterans: If claiming VEOA, VRA or 30% Disabled Veteran - Submit VOW certification memo or copy of the official DD-Form 214, which must include the character of service (i.e., with an honorable or general discharge). This will be annotated in block 24 on member copy 2, 4, or 7 of the DD-Form 214. If claiming 30% Disabled Veteran, you must also submit a VA Letter or a disability determination from a branch of the Armed Forces. NOTE: All veterans claiming 10-point preference must also submit a SF-15. Current or Former Federal Civilian Employees (includes current Air Force employees): You must submit a legible copy of a SF-50, Notification of Personnel Action. Promotion Consideration: If you wish to be considered as a promotion candidate and your SF-50 has an effective date within the past year, it may not clearly demonstrate you meet the one-year time-in-grade requirements.
